'''Sreenivasa Rao Jammalamadaka''', also known as '''J.S. Rao''',  is an Indian-American [[statistician]] who is a Distinguished Professor in the Department of [[Statistics]] and Applied Probability at the [[University of California, Santa Barbara]] (UCSB).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Statistics pioneer Sreenivasa Rao Jammalamadaka honored with lifetime achievement award {{!}} Division of Mathematical, Life and Physical Sciences |url=https://science.ucsb.edu/news/statistics-pioneer-sreenivasa-rao-jammalamadaka-honored-lifetime-achievement-award |access-date=2026-09-09 |website=science.ucsb.edu}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=UCSB |first=Harrison Tasoff for |date=2020-02-04 |title=Indian Society for Probability and Statistics Honors UCSB Professor |url=https://www.noozhawk.com/indian_society_for_probability_and_statistics_honors_ucsb_professor/ |access-date=2026-09-09 |website=Noozhawk |language=en-US}}</ref>  His research has focused on several areas including nonparametric statistical inference,<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last1=Jammalamadaka |first1=S. Rao |last2=Mangalam |first2=Vasudevan |date=2003 |title=Nonparametric estimation for middle-censored data |url=https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/1048525031000089266 |journal=Journal of Nonparametric Statistics |language=en |volume=15 |issue=2 |pages=253–265 |doi=10.1080/1048525031000089266 |issn=1048-5252|url-access=subscription }}</ref> goodness-of-fit testing,<ref name=":4">{{Cite journal |last1=Jammalamadaka |first1=Sreenivasa Rao |last2=Jiménez-Gamero |first2=M. Dolores |last3=Meintanis |first3=Simos G. |date=2019-12-17 |title=A class of goodness-of-fit tests for circular distributions based on trigonometric moments |url=https://raco.cat/index.php/SORT/article/view/361425 |journal=SORT-Statistics and Operations Research Transactions |language=en |volume=43 |issue=2 |pages=317–336 |issn=2013-8830}}</ref> [[Maximum spacing estimation|inference based on spacings]],<ref>{{Citation |last1=Ghosh |first1=Kaushik |title=Some Recent Results on Inference Based on Spacings |date=2000-12-31 |work=Asymptotics in Statistics and Probability |pages=185–196 |editor-last=Puri |editor-first=Madan L. |url=https://www.degruyterbrill.com/document/doi/10.1515/9783110942002-014/html |access-date=2026-09-09 |publisher=De Gruyter |doi=10.1515/9783110942002-014 |isbn=978-3-11-094200-2 |last2=Jammalamadaka |first2=S. Rao|url-access=subscription }}</ref> statistics of directional data in two- three- and higher dimensions,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Tasoff |first=Harrison |date=2020-02-03 |title=For Pioneering Contributions |url=https://news.ucsb.edu/2020/019777/pioneering-contributions |access-date=2026-09-09 |website=The Current |language=en}}</ref> probability and [[large-sample theory]],<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://shop.elsevier.com/books/probability-models/srinivasa-rao/978-0-443-29328-3 |title=Probability Models |date=2024-09-27 |isbn=978-0-443-29328-3 |language=en-US}}</ref> and [[linear models]].<ref name=":5">{{Cite book |last1=Sengupta |first1=Debasis |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Wv_UCgAAQBAJ |title=Linear Models: An Integrated Approach |last2=Jammalamadaka |first2=Sreenivasa Rao |date=2003-03-03 |publisher=World Scientific |isbn=978-981-4491-26-6 |language=en}}</ref> He has also worked on [[Bayesian inference]]<ref name=":6">{{Cite journal |last1=S |first1=Jammalamadaka |last2=Qianyu |first2=Jin |date=2022-12-23 |title=A Bayesian Test for the Number of Modes in a Gaussian Mixture |url=https://escholarship.org/uc/item/417768qs |journal=Department of Statistics and Applied Probability |language=en |archive-url=http://web.archive.org/web/20250324094429/https://escholarship.org/uc/item/417768qs |archive-date=2025-03-24}}</ref> and development of [[statistical methodology]] in disciplines such as [[geology]] and [[biology]]. He has held professional and visiting appointments at universities and research institutions in the United States, Europe, Australia, and Asia. His honors include fellowships of most major statistical societies and "Lifetime Achievement Awards" from the Indian Society for Probability and Statistics (2019)<ref name=":7">{{Cite web |title=Lifetime Achievement Awards {{!}} International Indian Statistical Association |url=https://www.intindstat.org/lifetime-awards |access-date=2026-09-09 |website=www.intindstat.org}}</ref> and most recently from the International Indian Statistical Association (2025).<ref>{{Cite web |title=2025 IISA Lifetime Achievement Award Winner {{!}} Statistics and Applied Probability |url=https://www.pstat.ucsb.edu/happenings/announcements/2025-iisa-lifetime-achievement-award-winner |access-date=2026-09-10 |website=www.pstat.ucsb.edu}}</ref>
==Early life and education==
{{unreferenced section|date=September 2026}}
Jammalamadaka was born in a small village called [[Munipalle, Uppalaguptam Mandal|Munipalle]], in [[Andhra Pradesh]], India. He was educated for a year at the YRS and VRN College in Chirala, followed by the [[Indian Statistical Institute]], Kolkata (B. Stat.1964, M.Stat. 1965, and Ph.D. 1969), while serving as a Research Scholar there during 1965-1969.

== Career ==
Jammalamadaka began his academic career at the Department of Mathematics, [[Indiana University, Bloomington]], where he served as a Visiting Assistant Professor and Assistant Professor from 1969 to 1976. In 1976, he joined the [[University of California, Santa Barbara]], as an Assistant Professor, progressing thro the ranks to become a Full Professor in 1983,<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=From the list of Past Presidents of SCASA: 1989-1990 Sreenivasa Rao Jammalamadaka, University of California, Santa Barbara |url=https://higherlogicdownload.s3.amazonaws.com/AMSTAT/a5245a58-1e57-4a63-a0f3-2bf1a84b7db7/UploadedImages/LeadershipLegacyCorner/LeadershipLegacyCorner_Issue1.pdf}}</ref> and was appointed to the special rank of Distinguished Professor in 2007.<ref name=":1" />

Jammalamadaka held visiting positions at the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]], the [[University of Leeds]], [[Uppsala University]], the [[Indian Statistical Institute]], the [[Indian Institute of Technology Bombay]], [[Chalmers University of Technology]], the [[University of Gothenburg]], the [[Australian National University]], the [[Curtin University of Technology]], the [[University of Malaya]], [[Karlsruhe Institute of Technology]], the [[University of Trento]], the [[University of Queensland]], the [[University of Geneva]], and the [[Gandhi Institute of Technology and Management]] (GITAM), in India.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title=Sreenivasa Rao Jammalamadaka {{!}} UCSB Center for Responsible Machine Learning |url=https://ml.ucsb.edu/people/faculty/sreenivasa-rao-jammalamadaka |access-date=2026-09-09 |website=ml.ucsb.edu |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":2" />

At UCSB, he served as vice-chairman of the Department of Mathematics, Director of the Statistical Consulting Center that he helped establish, Graduate Advisor in statistics, and as the first Chairman of the Department of Statistics and Applied Probability that he had a major role in getting started. He also served on several UCSB Academic Senate committees, including the Council on Planning and Budget, the Committee on Academic Personnel, and the Council on Faculty Issues and Awards.<ref name=":3" />

Jammalamadaka's doctoral students, numbering over 50 at this point, include such well-known names as Martin Wells at Cornell, and Siddhartha Chib at the Olin Business School in Washington Univ, St. Louis. They  have worked on topics including nonparametric testing, goodness-of-fit procedures, directional statistics, reliability theory, Bayesian methods, spatial statistics, financial modeling, image analysis, machine learning, and statistical inference. His teaching has included [[probability]], [[statistical theory]], [[sampling techniques]], [[order statistics]], [[experimental design]], [[time-series analysis]], [[multivariate analysis]], [[stochastic processes]], [[Directional data|directional data analysis]], [[Decision theory|statistical decision theory]], and [[nonparametric statistics]], besides math courses like [[calculus]] and [[linear algebra]].<ref>[https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=27204&fChrono=1 Ph.D. students on Math Genealogy]</ref>

Jammalamadaka is the author of over 200 publications and has written 3 scholarly books and edited conference proceedings and other special volumes \https://jammalam.faculty.pstat.ucsb.edu/. For his research guidance and mentoring activity at UCSB and worldwide, the University of California, SB recognized him in 2017 with an Outstanding Graduate Mentor Award.<ref>[http://www.pstat.ucsb.edu/news/announcement/1176 Outstanding Graduate Mentor Award]</ref> His students and co-workers brought out a [[Festschrift]] in his honor in 2011.<ref>[https://www.springer.com/us/book/9783790826272 Advances in Directional and Linear Statistics: A Festschrift for Sreenivasa Rao Jammalamadaka, Martin T. Wells and Ashis SenGupta (eds), Springer, 2011]</ref>

== Research and scholarly works ==
Jammalamadaka's research has covered several areas of [[Theoretical statistics|theoretical]] and [[applied statistics]]. His work includes [[Nonparametric statistics|nonparametric tests]],<ref name=":0" />, [[Asymptote|asymptotic efficiencies]]<ref name=":10">{{Cite journal |last1=Rao Jammalamadaka |first1=Sreenivasa |last2=Taufer |first2=Emanuele |last3=Terdik |first3=György H. |date=2021 |title=Asymptotic theory for statistics based on cumulant vectors with applications |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1111/sjos.12521 |journal=Scandinavian Journal of Statistics |language=en |volume=48 |issue=2 |pages=708–728 |doi=10.1111/sjos.12521 |issn=1467-9469|url-access=subscription }}</ref> statistical inference based on spacings, and statistical methods for circular and directional data.<ref>{{Cite book |title=Statistical Methods for Directional Data {{!}} Series on Multivariate Analysis |url=https://www.worldscientific.com/worldscibooks/10.1142/13189?srsltid=AfmBOorCbAJVaucodpKETGfeylWWc-_Nlde0i1F1Enri7nVv1P04y_x6 |access-date=2026-09-09 |via=www.worldscientific.com | date=2027 |language=en |doi=10.1142/13189 | isbn=978-981-12-6797-0 }}</ref> 

His work on [[directional statistics]] addressed inference for observations represented by directions or angles and included [[Goodness of fit|goodness-of-fit tests]],<ref name=":4" /> correlation and regression methods,<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Terdik |first1=Gy. |last2=Subba Rao |first2=T. |last3=Jammalamadaka |first3=S. Rao |date=2007 |title=On multivariate nonlinear regression models with stationary correlated errors |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S0378375807001358 |journal=Journal of Statistical Planning and Inference |language=en |volume=137 |issue=11 |pages=3793–3814 |doi=10.1016/j.jspi.2007.03.050}}</ref> and development of probability models for such data. His research interests also include limit distribution theory, asymptotic efficiencies of statistical tests, and linear models.{{cn|date=September 2026}}

A recurring theme in his research has been the use of spacings the differences between ordered observations in [[statistical inference]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Kochar |first=Subhash |date=2012 |title=Stochastic Comparisons of Order Statistics and Spacings: A Review |journal=International Scholarly Research Notices |language=en |volume=2012 |issue=1 |article-number=839473 |doi=10.5402/2012/839473 |doi-access=free |issn=2356-7872}}</ref> His publications have examined the asymptotic properties and efficiencies of tests based on spacings,<ref name=":10" /> including applications to goodness-of-fit and two-sample problems.<ref name=":4" /> 

Another major area of his work is directional and circular statistics.<ref>[https://www.springer.com/us/book/9783790826272 Advances in Directional and Linear Statistics: A Festschrift for Sreenivasa Rao Jammalamadaka, Martin T. Wells and Ashis SenGupta (eds), Springer, 2011]</ref> His research has included statistical inference for [[Circular distribution|circular distributions]], tests of uniformity, circular regression, wrapped probability distributions, skew-symmetric circular models, and statistical methods for spherical data.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Rao |first=Jammalamadaka, Sreenivasa |date=2017 |title=A General Approach for obtaining wrapped circular distributions via mixtures |url=https://escholarship.org/uc/item/5r7521z5 |journal=Sankhya |language=en |volume=79 |archive-url=http://web.archive.org/web/20240630021259/https://escholarship.org/uc/item/5r7521z5 |archive-date=2024-06-30}}</ref> Later work extended these methods to applications involving biological and medical data, including circular functional analysis of [[Optical Coherence Tomography]] (OCT) data, and analysis of [[retinal nerve fiber layer]] measurements to explore connections to problems like [[glaucoma]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Ali |first1=Md Hasnat |last2=Wainwright |first2=Brian |last3=Petersen |first3=Alexander |last4=Jonnadula |first4=Ganesh B. |last5=Desai |first5=Meghana |last6=Rao |first6=Harsha L. |last7=Srinivas |first7=M. B. |last8=Jammalamadaka |first8=S. Rao |last9=Senthil |first9=Sirisha |last10=Pyne |first10=Saumyadipta |date=2021-12-02 |title=Circular functional analysis of OCT data for precise identification of structural phenotypes in the eye |journal=Scientific Reports |volume=11 |issue=1 |pages=23336 |doi=10.1038/s41598-021-02025-4 |doi-access=free |issn=2045-2322 |pmc=8639843 |pmid=34857787 |bibcode=2021NatSR..1123336A }}</ref>

His research has also addressed goodness-of-fit testing, Bayesian and semiparametric inference, censored lifetime data, general linear models, multivariate statistics, time-series methods, and machine-learning-related statistical models. His publications include work on [[Bayesian structural time series|Bayesian structural time-series models]],<ref name=":6" /> mixture models,<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=J |first1=Frame, Samuel |last2=Rao |first2=Jammalamadaka, Sreenivasa |date=2007 |title=Generalized mixture models, semi-supervised learning, and unknown class inference |url=https://escholarship.org/uc/item/68h7q1v8 |journal=Advances in Data Analysis and Classification |language=en |volume=1 |issue=1 |pages=23–38 |doi= 10.1007/s11634-006-0001-9|issn=1862-5347 |archive-url=http://web.archive.org/web/20240414174024/https://escholarship.org/uc/item/68h7q1v8 |archive-date=2024-04-14}}</ref> [[Generalized linear model|generalized linear models]],<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Sengupta |first1=Debasis |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Wv_UCgAAQBAJ |title=Linear Models: An Integrated Approach |last2=Jammalamadaka |first2=Sreenivasa Rao |date=2003-03-03 |publisher=World Scientific |isbn=978-981-4491-26-6 |language=en}}</ref> lifetime-data analysis,<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Jammalamadaka |first1=S. Rao |last2=Leong |first2=Elvynna |date=2014-12-22 |title=Analysis of discrete lifetime data under middle-censoring and in the presence of covariates |url=https://escholarship.org/uc/item/8kp7n09t |journal=Journal of Applied Statistics |language=en |volume=42 |issue=4 |pages=905–913 |doi=10.1080/02664763.2014.993364 |issn=0266-4763 |archive-url=http://web.archive.org/web/20241214052715/https://escholarship.org/uc/item/8kp7n09t |archive-date=2024-12-14}}</ref> and statistical methods for multimodal and high-dimensional data. His later publications include studies of circular and spherical distributions,<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Jammalamadaka |first1=Sreenivasa Rao |last2=Meintanis |first2=Simos |last3=Verdebout |first3=Thomas |date=2020-08-01 |title=On Sobolev tests of uniformity on the circle with an extension to the sphere |url=https://projecteuclid.org/journals/bernoulli/volume-26/issue-3/On-Sobolev-tests-of-uniformity-on-the-circle-with-an/10.3150/19-BEJ1191.full |journal=Bernoulli |volume=26 |issue=3 |doi=10.3150/19-BEJ1191 |issn=1350-7265|hdl=2013/ULB-DIPOT:oai:dipot.ulb.ac.be:2013/335341 |hdl-access=free }}</ref> multivariate skewness<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Rao |first1=Jammalamadaka, Sreenivasa |last2=Emanuele |first2=Taufer |last3=H |first3=Terdik, Gyorgy |date=2021 |title=On Multivariate Skewness and Kurtosis |url=https://escholarship.org/uc/item/5bk0b7qm |journal=Sankhya A |language=en |volume=83 |issue=2 |doi= |issn=0976-836X |archive-url=http://web.archive.org/web/20240910143007/https://escholarship.org/uc/item/5bk0b7qm |archive-date=2024-09-10}}</ref> and [[kurtosis]], and applications of circular statistics to biological data as in chronobiology.

He has authored or coauthored books including ''Essential Statistics'' (1998), ''Topics in Circular Statistics'' (2001),<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Jammalamadaka |first1=S. Rao |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=sKqWMGqQXQkC |title=Topics in Circular Statistics |last2=Sengupta |first2=Ambar |last3=Sengupta |first3=Ashis |date=2001 |publisher=World Scientific |isbn=978-981-277-926-7 |language=en}}</ref> ''Linear Models, An Integrated Approach'' (2003),<ref name=":5" /> ''Essential Statistics with Python and R'' (2019), and ''Linear Models and Regression with R'' (2019).<ref>{{Cite book |last1=JAMMALAMADAKA (DEBASIS.) |first1=S. RAO SENGUPTA |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=_1g8zQEACAAJ |title=Linear Models and Regression with R: An Integrated Approach |last2=Sengupta |first2=Debasis |date=2019 |publisher=World Scientific Publishing Company Pte. Limited |isbn=978-981-12-0041-0 |language=en}}</ref>

Jammalamadaka has served on editorial boards of several statistical journals.{{cn|date=September 2026}} He founded and directed the Statistical Consulting Center (StatLab) at UCSB and has provided statistical consulting on problems ranging from environmental studies and engineering to medical and biological research.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dr. S. Rao J. |url=https://jammalam.faculty.pstat.ucsb.edu/html/professional_activities.htm |access-date=2026-09-09 |website=jammalam.faculty.pstat.ucsb.edu}}</ref>
